findings.finding: Markedly impaired: set-shifting (Trail Making Test B), abstraction (similarities) and response inhibition; perseverative errors on card sorting.
Letter (phonemic) fluency reduced out of proportion to category fluency.
Impaired emotion recognition (Ekman faces) and theory-of-mind (faux pas) performance; reduced affective empathy on the Interpersonal Reactivity Index (informant).
Relatively spared: encoding and free recall reduced in a retrieval pattern, with comparatively preserved recognition and cued recall.
Preserved. Copy of complex figure and clock contour intact; errors, when present, reflect poor planning rather than a perceptual or constructional deficit.
Fluent speech; single-word comprehension intact; confrontation naming largely preserved; no agrammatism.
Reduced insight (anosognosia), stimulus-bound responses, and reduced concern for test performance noted during the session.
Euthymic by report; no manic or depressive features at testing. Word-for-word story repetition observed during the session.

output.impression: 1. Marked executive and social-cognition impairment with phonemic fluency reduced more than category fluency. 2. Episodic memory relatively spared, with preserved recognition. 3. Visuospatial and constructional function preserved. 4. Reduced insight; euthymic at testing. The profile is executive and social-cognitive predominant with relative sparing of memory recognition and visuospatial function, consistent with a frontal-network syndrome.

action_criteria.rationale: Excludes metabolic, endocrine, nutritional and inflammatory contributors before attributing decline to neurodegeneration.

action_criteria.rationale: Twenty years of lithium with an eGFR of 64 and a new cognitive-behavioural syndrome make chronic lithium toxicity a reversible mimic to exclude.

action_criteria.label: MRI brain without contrast, dementia protocol
action_criteria.rationale: Shows the frontal and anterior temporal atrophy pattern and excludes structural and vascular causes.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right-predominant frontal and anterior temporal hypometabolism or hypoperfusion with posterior sparing
action_criteria.label: FDG-PET when the structural picture is unresolved
action_criteria.rationale: Frontal and anterior temporal hypometabolism with posterior sparing supports FTD over AD.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Identifies or excludes a pathogenic C9orf72, GRN or MAPT variant relevant to prognosis and to relatives

action_criteria.rationale: Onset about 64 without a suggestive family history: the FTD consortium advises C9orf72 screening in possible or probable bvFTD, UK eligibility does not, so a counselled panel is optional.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD, NICE NG97 advises against it, and it may worsen behaviour.
Do not start memantine: a randomised trial showed no benefit in FTD and NICE NG97 advises against it.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
Do not stop lithium abruptly: abrupt discontinuation raises the risk of manic relapse; any dose change is made with his psychiatrist and guided by levels and renal function.
required_recommendations: Apply the Rascovsky 2011 criteria: state which features are present, the functional decline, and the level of certainty (possible or probable).

Explain why the syndrome is not lithium toxicity or a bipolar relapse: the level of 1.28 mmol/L is only mildly above range without tremor, ataxia, myoclonus or confusion, and his son describes a euthymic, qualitatively new syndrome of apathy, stereotyped repetition and impulsivity over 16 months.

With his psychiatrist, bring the lithium level back into the maintenance range (dose review given eGFR 64), recheck the level and renal function, and advise avoiding dehydration, NSAIDs and other drugs that raise lithium.
Address safety and capacity: he lives alone, so supervision of lithium and other medicines, driving, finances (impulsive purchases) and lasting power of attorney while he can still take part.
Arrange caregiver education and support, and a plan for behavioural symptoms that avoids cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not part of the FTD work-up; FDG-PET, or perfusion SPECT where FDG-PET is unavailable, is the functional study when one is needed.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

accepted: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), probable, sporadic, comorbid bipolar disorder type I (stable on lithium)

differential.key_features: For: level 1.28 mmol/L with eGFR 64. Against: no tremor, ataxia, myoclonus, dysarthria or confusion; a 16-month frontal behavioural syndrome with frontal atrophy is not a toxic encephalopathy.
Against: euthymic by patient and son, who knows his episodes and calls this different; no admission for 12 years; stereotyped repetition and loss of interest rather than mood change.
Against: frontal-predominant atrophy with posterior sparing and preserved recognition memory.
Coronary disease and diabetes, but only Fazekas 1 white matter change and no infarct.

key_clinical_evidence: Son's history over 16 months: verbatim repetition of the same stories, loss of interest in architecture and friends, impulsive purchases, little response to his grandchildren and hygiene decline, without insight.
Euthymic throughout by patient and son; the son, who knows his bipolar episodes, calls this qualitatively different; no admission for 12 years.
Lithium 1.28 mmol/L is mildly above the maintenance range without tremor, ataxia, myoclonus or confusion; it needs correction but does not explain the syndrome.
MRI: right-predominant frontal and mild anterior temporal atrophy with preserved posterior cortex and minimal white matter change.
The frontal and anterior temporal pattern with relative posterior sparing makes Alzheimer disease less likely; an amyloid or CSF AD biomarker study is optional if doubt remains.

clinical_assessment.impression: 5 of the 6 Rascovsky features are present on informant history and examination (disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy, perseverative behaviour and an executive-predominant profile), with documented decline in daily function. This meets possible bvFTD; imaging and neuropsychological testing decide whether it is probable. Memory and visuospatial function are relatively preserved on the bedside screen.

Behavioural variant frontotemporal demen.summary: Rascovsky and colleagues (2011) define possible behavioural variant FTD by three of six behavioural and cognitive features, probable bvFTD by added functional decline and frontal or anterior temporal involvement on structural or functional imaging, and definite bvFTD by histopathology or a pathogenic mutation. New behavioural change in mid-life with progressive functional decline should prompt a neurodegenerative work-up even in a person with a psychiatric history. Treatment is supportive: SSRIs or trazodone for behaviour, caregiver support and safety planning; cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are not recommended.

metadata.notes: Probable bvFTD in a 66-year-old man with bipolar disorder stable on lithium for 20 years and CKD stage 2. Key teaching: a mildly raised lithium level is a reversible contributor to check and correct, but a euthymic, qualitatively new syndrome with stereotyped repetition, apathy and frontal atrophy is not explained by lithium or by bipolar disorder.

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. E is a 66-year-old retired architect with a 20-year history of bipolar disorder type I (well-controlled on lithium for 20 years) who presents with his son for evaluation of progressive behavioral and cognitive changes. His son, who visits weekly and is familiar with his father's bipolar episodes, specifically states: 'this is NOT a mood episode — he's not manic, he's not depressed, this is different.' Over the past 16 months, his father has begun repeating verbatim the same stories from childhood in virtually every conversation — the same three anecdotes, word for word, regardless of whether they are contextually appropriate. He has lost interest in architecture and design, which defined his entire career and retirement. He no longer visits his former colleagues or attends architecture events he previously attended religiously. He has made increasingly impulsive small purchases — nothing major, but he bought 30 identical coffee mugs because they were 'on sale,' which his son found bizarre. His hygiene has declined. He has become socially withdrawn, showing little response when his grandchildren call. He does not recognize these changes in himself. The bipolar disorder has been stable — his last hospitalization was 12 years ago, and his mood has been euthymic by both patient and caregiver reports throughout this period. He has coronary artery disease (status post stenting 8 years ago) and type 2 diabetes. He has CKD stage 2 with eGFR 64.
